pages.text: $(item)Coax$() carries the signal from the radio to the antenna. Lay it like redstone: it climbs walls and hangs from ceilings. One radio per antenna: two radios or two antennas on one coax run $(thing)overdraw$() and nothing works.$(br2)With nothing on its coax a radio still reaches about $(thing)8 blocks$() from its bare connector.

A $(item)balun$() joins coax to antenna wire, and its ratio decides the antenna:$(li)$(thing)1:1$(): dipole, inverted V, end-fed, vertical$(li)$(thing)2:1$(): quad loops$(li)$(thing)4:1$(): off-centre-fed dipole$(li)$(thing)9:1$(): random wire
pages.title: Baluns
Coloured coax
pages.text: Coax comes in sixteen colours. Coax joins only coax of its own colour (plain is a colour of its own), so runs of different colours can lie side by side and stay apart (a $(l:radiocraft:direction_finding/direction_finder)direction finder$(/l) needs this). Plain coax joins any colour.$(br2)Use a dye on laid coax to colour the whole run, or sneak to colour one block. Recipes that take coax want plain coax.

pages.title: Bundles
pages.text: Use a wire item of another kind on laid coax (or coax on a wire) and both lie in the same block: a $(item)Wire Bundle$() of up to seven cables, power wire, $(l:radiocraft:radios/data_wire)data wire$(/l) and any colours of coax, drawn side by side. Each cable keeps its own links, so a bundle behind a radio can carry its power wire and its coax out together and part them wherever you like.$(br2)Sneak + right click a bundle with an empty hand to take out the cable under the crosshair; breaking it drops them all. Dye recolours the coax under the crosshair.
